_comment: The patcher window's "?" guides. One short, plain guide for every patch (by patch id) and every button, tool and setting (by control key). Each guide is a list of short lines: what it does, how to use it, and what to watch out for. tests/test_how_to_use.py refuses a patch or control without one, and a guide that is too long or uses technical words. Same style as the Virtual Villagers Fun Patcher's guides.

guide: Fixes three small bugs of the original game.
A brand-new family is kept even if the game is closed without Quit (a crash, say). Power Failure now tells the truth about the food. A cheat-set age no longer counts as the Oldest Villager record.
Nothing to click: tick it, patch, and play as usual.
On by default.
Changes only the yearly roll for dying of old age, using the curve from Virtual Families 2.
There is no fixed maximum age any more: villagers can live well past 100, though it becomes more and more likely that they die.
Nothing to click: tick it, patch, and play as usual.
Because parents can live on, Next Generation is also offered once the oldest parent at home is 60 and a child survives.
A married man and woman with six children can still have private romantic time (the game said "They have enough kids already!").
Drop one of them on the other, as usual. No baby is possible for them.
A couple that cannot have a baby is never made to wait before trying again.
Mothers over 50 can still become pregnant: 10% at 50, falling to a permanent 0.1% from 69.
Nothing to click: tick it, patch, and play as usual.
Below 50 the game's own chances are unchanged.
Keeps coins at 4,000,000,000 or less and food at 2,147,483,647 or less, the Virtual Families 2 maximums.
Without it, food past that number wraps around to a negative number and glitches the game.
Nothing to click: tick it, patch, and play as usual.
Adds Special Upgrades to the new Upgrades button in the store: Brokerage Account, Food Club, Health Plan and Lucky Rock.
It also adds a Maid and a Gardener who keep the house and yard clean.
Each one asks you to confirm and then shows Purchased. Buying one again removes it, with no refund.
Adds cheat pages to the Upgrades button in the store: money, food, the bank's interest rate, villager cheats, store prices, achievements, house and yard mess, time controls and the Family page.
Click Upgrades next to Done in the store, then pick a page. Every cheat button asks you to confirm.
Cheat money does not count toward the money achievements.
Back up your saves first if you plan to experiment: use Back Up Saves on the Tools tab.
Adds a Flea Market page to the Upgrades button with every tray item the store sells.
Click an item to buy it, or to get it for free.
Buying one again removes it, as with the Special Upgrades.
Adds a Roll the Dice page to the Upgrades button.
It costs $500 and an island event happens right away.
Anything can happen, good or bad. Back up your saves first if you care about the family.
Replaces the standard house and some game pictures with customized ones, made by the fans at LDWForums.
Pictures only: gameplay and saves are not touched.
Untick it and patch again to get the original pictures back.
Adds the songs of Virtual Families 2 to the songs of Virtual Families 1.
Nothing to click: the game plays them with its own.
Untick it and patch again to get only the original songs.
Makes the collectables in the yard glow, so they are easier to spot.
Pictures only: gameplay and saves are not touched.
Untick it and patch again to get the original look back.
The caption under a villager now varies, using the captions of Virtual Families 2: TV, reading, the web, video games, board games, homework, the sandbox, naps, the pool and more.
At the computer, browsing the web and playing video games are chosen 50:50.
Only the words change: what villagers do, and how often, stays the game's own.
One generation may have up to 28 children instead of 6. Only the first 6 appear in the Family Tree, but any child can be chosen to inherit the house.
Nothing to click. Children 7 to 28 are remembered in a small file beside each save; the save itself is not changed.
Experimental: not yet tested in a running game. It is never ticked by Enable All; tick it yourself.
Back up your saves before using it: use Back Up Saves on the Tools tab.
Keeps logs of your family as you play: Family History, Births and Conceptions, Deaths with their cause, Events, Population and Statistics.
Each save slot gets its own folder, Virtual Families 1 Patcher\Save N, beside your saves.
A family started before this patch gets its earlier generations added once from the family tree, marked "backfilled, no date".
Starting over or a new family clears that slot's logs (backups are kept); evicting the family keeps them.
Experimental: not yet tested in a running game. It is never ticked by Enable All; tick it yourself.

getting_started.title: Getting started
guide: The patcher makes a separate modded copy of your Virtual Families folder. Your original game and saves are never changed.
On the Patches tab: choose your vanilla Virtual Families folder, tick the patches you want, then click Enable/Disable Patches.
Play "Virtual Families - Modded.exe" inside the new modded folder. The Upgrades button is next to Done in the store.
The Tools tab has Back Up Saves and Restore Saves for your family saves.
Every "?" button explains the feature beside it.

game_folder.title: Vanilla game folder
guide: Click Browse and pick your official Virtual Families folder, the one that holds Virtual Families.exe.
Leave it empty to only change the patches of a modded folder you already made: choose that one under Modded output folder.
The original folder is only read, never changed.

patch_manifest.title: Patch manifest
guide: The list of patches and their settings. The patcher fills it in for you when it starts.
You only need Browse if you were given another list to try.
Load Manifest Settings shows its patches below.

output_location.title: Modded output location
guide: Save modified folders under: the folder where "Virtual Families - Modded" is made. Leave it empty to use the folder next to your game (or your Games folder if the game is under Program Files).
Modded output folder: the finished modded game. Choose an existing one here to change its patches without the vanilla folder.

backup_folder.title: Backup folder and patch log
guide: Backup folder: where the patcher keeps a copy of the old modded folder before each rebuild. Leave it empty for the default.
Patch log: where a record of the run is written. Leave it empty for the default.
These are game-file backups, not save backups. For your saves use Back Up Saves on the Tools tab.

load_manifest.title: Load Manifest Settings
guide: Reads the patch list again and shows each patch with a checkbox and a short description.
A patch that needs another says so in bold, and ticking it ticks the other one too.

defaults.title: Defaults
guide: Ticks the patches that are on by default.
The Experimental ones are left unticked.

enable_all.title: Enable All
guide: Ticks every patch except the Experimental ones, which you tick yourself.
Click Enable/Disable Patches afterwards to apply it.

disable_all.title: Disable All
guide: Unticks every patch, so you can tick just the ones you want.
Applying it gives you the original game in a modded folder.

enable_main.title: Enable All Main Patches
guide: Ticks every patch under Main Patches and leaves the others as they are.
Click Enable/Disable Patches afterwards to apply it.

enable_optional.title: Enable all Optional Content
guide: Ticks every patch under Optional Patches and leaves the others as they are.
Click Enable/Disable Patches afterwards to apply it.

dry_run.title: Dry Run (Validate Only)
guide: Checks that your game folder is the right one and that the patches fit, without writing anything.
Worth a click before the first real run.
The Run Log shows the result.

enable_disable.title: Enable/Disable Patches
guide: Makes or refreshes the modded game with the ticked patches on and the unticked ones off.
With a vanilla folder chosen, the modded folder is rebuilt from it. With only a modded folder chosen, its patches are switched in place.
It first backs up the files it will change; Restore backup undoes a run.
It asks you to confirm.

restore_backup.title: Restore Backup
guide: Puts the modded folder back the way it was before one Enable/Disable run.
Click Browse and pick a folder inside .vf1_patch_backups, then click Restore Backup. It asks first.
This is for the game files. To put back your saves use Restore Saves on the Tools tab.

check_for_updates.title: Check for updates
guide: Opens the patcher's page on GitHub in your browser, where the newest version is.
Nothing is downloaded or changed by the click.

back_up_saves.title: Back Up Saves
guide: Copies your family saves, and the patcher's own files for each save, into a dated Backups folder inside the save folder.
Click Back Up Saves, tick the save folders you want, then Back Up Selected.
The game can stay open: it is paused for the copy, but the backup holds the family as of its last save.
Old backups are never replaced or deleted. Every copy is checked against the original.

restore_saves.title: Restore Saves
guide: Puts a backup back: the whole save folder, or one save slot.
One slot means that slot's save, its two older autosave copies, its patcher data and its Children files. The shared options file and the engine log are only restored with the whole folder.
Quit the game first, from its own menu.
Choose a backup, choose whole folder or one slot, then Restore...; you are shown what will change and asked to confirm first.
Your saves as they are now are backed up first, so a restore can be undone.
Delete Backup... removes a backup you no longer want (it asks first).

rename_family.title: Rename Family
guide: Changes a family's name in its save, so the slot menu and the game show the new name.
Quit the game first, from its own menu. Click Rename Family..., pick the save, type the new name (1 to 19 characters, the most the game keeps), then Rename.
Your saves are backed up first, as "Backup <date> (before rename)", so it can be undone with Restore Saves.
Letters, digits and spaces are safe. Which other symbols the game can draw is not yet confirmed, so an odd symbol may show wrongly.
Old logs keep their history and their old name. New log files use the new name, and the Family History gets one line saying the family was renamed.

game_speed.title: Game Speed
guide: Pauses or unpauses a family in its save, the same way the game's own Pause Game option does.
Quit the game first, from its own menu. Click Game Speed..., pick the save (each shows its speed now), choose Paused or Normal, then Set Speed.
Paused works as if you paused just before the game last saved. Normal works as if you unpaused it right now, so the time it spent paused is never aged in.
Set Normal just before you play: like any family at normal speed, it catches up on the time the game is closed after that.
Your saves are backed up first, as "Backup <date> (before speed change)", so Restore Saves can undo it.
Time Controls' Slow, Fast, 5x and 10x are not offered: the game never keeps them in a save and loads every family at Normal or Paused.
A save at any other speed is shown but not changed here; change it in the game instead.

game_mechanics.title: Game Mechanics
guide: Shows how Virtual Families works underneath: ageing, time away, needs, health, sickness, old age, babies, careers, money, events, messes and more.
Click Game Mechanics... and pick a topic at the top to jump to it. Every time is a real time, for Normal speed, with Slow and Fast beside it.
Each line says how sure it is: VERIFIED-E (the game's own code was run), VERIFIED-C (read in the game's own code) or UNCONFIRMED.
It only reads: no save or game file is opened or changed, so the game can stay open.

family_tree.title: Family Tree Maker
guide: Draws a family's tree from its save: every generation's parents and children, with each face from the game.
Click Family Tree Maker, choose the save folder and the family, then Open. Pick the game folder too, or each face shows a letter.
Click a portrait to edit its words, shape, colour and marks. Save keeps your tree for next time; Export as Picture saves a PNG or JPG.
The game forgets a divorced spouse, a first spouse after a new marriage, and a parent who died with no children. The tree remembers them, but only if it was opened while they were still in the save.
With the Family Logs patch on, twins, causes of death and past marriages show too. Without it the tree says what is not known.
Your saves are only read, never changed.
